title: Wave models on GPUs: C++/Kokkos and Rust ports of WAVEWATCH III that must give the Fortran's bits
description:
A preprint, v0, not peer reviewed. It claims no speed-up.

The project exists to support Ondas & Ventos (https://ondaseventos.ufsc.br/), the operational WAVEWATCH III forecast that LabECO/UFSC runs for ReNOMO, which must run the wave model at each cycle and plans to force it with several wind models.

We report two ports of the WAVEWATCH III (WW3) spectral wave model. Coding agents wrote both ports, and both ports have one acceptance rule: the port must give the same bits as the Fortran. A tolerance is a diagnostic, never the verdict. ww3-gpu keeps WW3, and the Fortran calls C++ written with Kokkos, behind one run-time flag for each routine. Its reference is the Fortran path of the same executable. chaceon replaces WW3 with Rust, compiled for the CPU, for SPIR-V (rust-gpu) and for PTX (Rust-CUDA). No Fortran runs in its process, and its reference is a WW3 that is compiled separately. ww3-gpu ports the discrete interaction approximation (DIA) of the four-wave transfer. On the CPU, it is byte-identical on all 100 serial and 25 OpenMP entries of the WW3 regression matrix that select it. The DIA takes 48.4 % of single-thread self time on a case of 9 520 points. chaceon runs ww3_grid, ww3_strt, ww3_prep and ww3_shel without Fortran, and 96 output files are byte-identical to the reference. Neither port has run the whole model on a real GPU. We compare how each project defines and checks its evidence.

The record holds the English paper and its edition in Brazilian Portuguese (Português Técnico Controlado). Source: marola-research, wave-models-on-gpus.
